title: Topological Splitting of Sondheimer Oscillations in Thin-Film Weyl Semimetals
abstract: We discuss topological effects on Sondheimer oscillations in the magnetoresistance of thin-film Weyl semimetals. The Sondheimer oscillations are periodic in magnetic field and originate from the commensurability between the film thickness and the cyclotron-orbit pitch. Using Boltzmann transport theory, we investigate the effects of Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment on the oscillations. We find that the Sondheimer oscillations split into two branches with different frequencies and that each branch becomes chirped because its frequency depends on magnetic field. These features originate from the orbital-Zeeman-induced deformation of the Fermi surface. The same mechanism also applies to Dirac semimetals.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how topological properties, specifically the Berry curvature in Weyl semimetals, alter the standard Sondheimer oscillations in magnetoresistance. The key finding is that these oscillations split into two distinct, chirping branches due to the orbital-Zeeman-induced deformation of the Fermi surface. This provides a measurable signature of topological physics in transport measurements.
main_problem: The paper investigates how topological effects modify the characteristic Sondheimer oscillations (SOs) observed in the magnetoresistance of thin-film Weyl semimetals.
main_result: The topological correction causes the SOs to split into two distinct branches, and furthermore, each branch exhibits a 'chirp' where its frequency depends on the applied magnetic field.
method: The analysis employs Boltzmann transport theory, incorporating semiclassical dynamics and calculating the oscillatory contributions to conductivity and resistivity.
model_or_system: The system is a thin-film Weyl semimetal, modeled using a Hamiltonian describing a single isotropic Weyl cone. The key physics involves the coupling between electron motion and the Berry curvature, leading to an orbital Zeeman effect that deforms the Fermi surface.
key_observables: Transverse magnetoresistance ($ho_{xx}$), the oscillatory component ($\deltaho_{xx}$), and the frequency separation/chirp observed in Fourier power spectra.
important_parameters: The dimensionless topological parameter $b_k = eB/(k\Omega\hbar)$, the film thickness ($L$), and the Fermi wavevector ($k_F$).
main_assumptions: Assumes constant bulk relaxation time ($	au$) and completely diffusive surface scattering. Calculations are performed retaining terms up to first order in $b_k$.
figures_summary: Figures show the origin of SOs via commensurability, the deformed Fermi surface, and numerical results demonstrating the splitting of the oscillation peak into two components whose separation increases with the magnetic field (chirping).
paper_structure: The paper builds from the physical origin of SOs, develops the theoretical framework using Boltzmann transport theory modified by topological terms, derives the resulting oscillatory behavior, and concludes with numerical verification of the splitting and chirping effects.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the study of topological band structures and their observable signatures (like the splitting/chirping) provides a theoretical framework for understanding how Berry curvature manifests in macroscopic transport measurements, which is relevant to topological quantum materials research.
